public.landing.title: Save it, don’t waste it.
public.landing.lead: You pick up what bakeries, shops and restaurants near you would otherwise throw away – and share it with the people around you. Voluntary, free of charge, together with many others.
public.landing.mission.title: What it’s about
public.landing.mission.text: Every day good food ends up in the bin – in shops, bakeries, restaurants and at home. You pick it up before that happens and share it with people near you. No money, no obligation, together with many others. Since 2012, run by volunteers, ad-free and open source.
public.landing.way.member.title: As a foodsaver
public.landing.way.member.text: You pick up what businesses can no longer sell and take it to where it gets eaten.
public.landing.way.home.title: At home
public.landing.way.home.text: Cooked too much or going on holiday? Offer a food basket or bring it to a Fairteiler.
public.landing.way.business.title: As a business
public.landing.way.business.text: You run a shop or a restaurant? We pick up reliably – free of charge and with a liability waiver.
public.landing.art.fsp.mainSub: Open to everyone · no account needed
public.landing.art.business.mainSub: Your team: just set it aside
public.explainer.journeyLead: Four steps. The first three online, whenever you like – then you head out with experienced foodsavers.
public.landing.step.1.title: Create an account
public.landing.step.1.text: With an email link, Google or a passkey. No password needed.
public.landing.step.2.title: Learn the basics
public.landing.step.2.text: The foodsharing basics: principles, code of conduct, hygiene rules, legal agreement – read at your pace, look up any time.
public.landing.step.3.title: Foodsaver quiz
public.landing.step.3.text: Online, whenever you like. Several attempts are fine.
public.landing.step.4.title: Intro pickups & ID
public.landing.step.4.text: At least three pickups with experienced foodsavers. Your ambassador checks your ID once – then you get your foodsaver ID card.
public.landing.step.4.duration: depends on dates in your district
public.landing.step.end: You pick up on your own

public.landing.near.lead: Districts are our local groups, Fairteiler are public fridges and shelves. Find both around the corner.

public.landing.fairteiler.title: What is a Fairteiler?
public.landing.fairteiler.text: A Fairteiler is a public fridge or shelf. Everyone may bring and take food – no account, no questions. Foodsavers fill it with rescued food and keep it clean.
public.landing.fairteiler.rule1: Bring what you would still eat yourself
public.landing.business.lead: We pick up what you can no longer sell. You set it aside – vetted foodsavers from your area take care of everything else.
public.landing.business.benefit.free.tex: No fees, no fixed-term contract. Nothing is resold – the food is given away.
public.landing.business.benefit.cost.tex: Less in the container, fewer collections, lower fees.
public.landing.business.benefit.staff.ti: No extra work for your team
public.landing.business.benefit.staff.te: Foodsavers sort, pack and carry everything away themselves.
public.landing.business.benefit.accept.t: Past best-before date, dairy, day-old bread, damaged packaging.
public.landing.business.benefit.reliable: Fixed pickup times, early or late, Saturdays and Sundays. If someone drops out, the team steps in.
public.landing.business.benefit.liabilit: Every foodsaver signs it in our legal agreement – before their first pickup.
public.landing.business.quote: “Since we started working with foodsharing, the container is half empty in the evening – and the team goes home on time.”
public.landing.business.quoteBy: Owner of a bakery in Zurich (example quote)
public.landing.moreWays.title: More ways to help
public.landing.moreWays.lead: foodsharing is run by volunteers, independent, ad-free and open source. There is more than one way to be part of it.
public.landing.moreWays.basket.title: Food baskets
public.landing.moreWays.basket.text: Cooked too much? Offer a food basket – someone from the neighbourhood picks it up.
public.landing.moreWays.donate.title: Donate
public.landing.moreWays.donate.text: foodsharing is run by volunteers and ad-free. Your donation pays for servers, insurance and material.
public.landing.moreWays.it.title: IT & helping out
public.landing.moreWays.it.text: The platform is open source. Code, design, translation or press work – you’re welcome.
public.landing.duties.title: Your commitments
public.landing.duties.lead: Foodsharing works because businesses can rely on us. That’s why you promise a few things – nothing more.
public.landing.duties.noTitle: What you don’t have to do
public.landing.duties.reliable.title: Be reliable
public.landing.duties.reliable.text: You only sign up when you’re sure you’ll come. If it doesn’t work out, you sign off early and find a replacement.
public.landing.duties.take.title: Take everything, throw nothing away
public.landing.duties.take.text: You take everything edible and pass on what you don’t need – to people or to a Fairteiler.
public.landing.duties.nosale.title: Sell nothing
public.landing.duties.nosale.text: Rescued food is given away, never sold or traded.
public.landing.duties.conduct.title: Be friendly at the business
public.landing.duties.conduct.text: On time, with your foodsaver ID, no arguing about amount or kind – and you leave everything clean.
public.landing.duties.privacy.title: Keep things confidential
public.landing.duties.privacy.text: You don’t pass on other foodsavers’ data or internal information.
public.landing.duties.not.min.title: No minimum number of pickups
public.landing.duties.not.min.text: You decide yourself how often you take part.
public.landing.duties.not.money.title: No costs, no contract
public.landing.duties.not.money.text: You can pause or stop at any time.
public.landing.duties.not.alone.title: Never alone at the start
public.landing.duties.not.alone.text: You do your first pickups with experienced foodsavers.
public.landing.duties.rules: Read all rules in the wiki
public.explainer.faq.what.a: You pick up food from businesses that would otherwise end up in the bin – and make sure it gets eaten: by you, your neighbours or via a Fairteiler.
public.explainer.faq.who.a: Everyone aged 18 or over with an official ID. You don’t need any prior knowledge – you learn everything along the way.
public.explainer.faq.cost.a: No. foodsharing is run by volunteers, free of charge and ad-free. You pay nothing, and you don’t get paid either.
public.explainer.faq.time.q: How much time do I need?
public.explainer.faq.time.a: The three online steps take a little over an hour in total, and you can read in several sittings. After that you decide yourself when and how often you pick up.
public.explainer.faq.id.q: What do I need to get started?
public.explainer.faq.id.a: An email address or a Google account. For the foodsaver ID card your ambassador checks your official ID once – nobody keeps a copy.
public.explainer.faq.duties.a: In short: be reliable, take everything, sell nothing, be friendly. The full list is above under “Your commitments”.
public.explainer.faq.cancel.q: What if I can’t make a pickup?
public.explainer.faq.cancel.a: Sign off as early as possible and let your team know. Less than 24 hours before, you also call so someone can step in.
public.explainer.faq.all.q: Do I have to take everything?
public.explainer.faq.all.a: Yes, everything edible the business gives you – unless something else was agreed. What you don’t need, you pass on.
public.explainer.faq.safe.a: Only what is still edible is rescued. In the learning pages and the quiz you learn what to watch out for: cold chain, shelf life, packaging.
public.explainer.faq.fairteiler.a: A public fridge or shelf. Everyone may put food in or take it out – no account needed.
public.explainer.faq.basket.q: Can I take part without pickups?
public.explainer.faq.basket.a: Yes. With a food basket you offer your own food or pick some up from others. All you need is an account, no quiz.
public.explainer.faq.business.q: I run a business – how do I become a partner?
public.explainer.faq.business.a: Write to us via “Become a partner” above. Your district gets in touch and agrees times and procedures with you.
